account:
Today seems quiet from what I have personally heard and seen. I kept my morning office business, market walk, noon lunch, town accounts appointment and afternoon tea. The treasury held 128 emeralds, and the secretary said no further bills, council papers or correspondence had reached her. Near town hall I heard residents asking the builder for an update on town works, but I have not heard an answer or learned of any particular project or problem.

The innkeeper requested a meeting tomorrow at eighteen in the great hall about the inn's service to the town, and agreed to meet me at my office at seventeen forty-five so we can walk over together. The secretary was asked to record it. I do not yet know the proposal or why the innkeeper wants that discussion; the request alone does not establish anything unusual.

At tea, the neighbour said the riverside has been peaceful, with no trouble personally seen and no request for town hall. The neighbour also passed on the baker's message that fresh bread would be at the market stall today. That sounds like ordinary advertising, not evidence of a wider issue. I have said goodbye and am still at the cottage; it is now sixteen-oh-seven, and I should return to the office for sixteen-thirty. Tomorrow's appointment book also calls for a ten o'clock grain inspection at the mill.
